meta.note: Derived from the analyst workbook, which is fed by the same Yardi/RealPage reports the Drive pipeline collects. Refresh by pasting new reports into the workbook's grey Source tabs, recalculating in Excel, and re-running scripts/extract_landing.py.

expense_noi.tax_note: April 2026 real estate tax true-up distorts that month; TTM run-rate for taxes is ~172.5k/mo. Whether the April entry is a one-off or an under-accrual catch-up is an open question — see the tax-accrual readings.

expense_overview.period_note: Matching periods: January to July 2026 against January to July 2025, so the comparison is genuinely year over year. Trailing-twelve-month figures and per-unit use the full TTM window. Status reflects direction of travel, not absolute level.

buckets.name: Real estate & other taxes
buckets.read: Up on the April entry alone. The monthly accrual never changed. Unresolved and material.

buckets.name: Payroll & benefits
buckets.read: Down year on year despite the January reclassification into supervisor and assistant manager lines.

buckets.name: Contract services
buckets.read: Elevator repair and a new water quality contract drive most of it. Confirm whether either recurs.

buckets.name: Management fee
buckets.read: Moves with revenue by contract. Nothing to manage here.

buckets.name: Insurance
buckets.read: Up double digits, in line with the wider market. Worth testing at renewal but largely non-controllable.

buckets.name: Administrative
buckets.read: Memberships and dues is the largest single line. Ask what it covers.

buckets.name: Repairs & maintenance
buckets.read: Up sharply on matching periods, driven by carpets, doors and glass, and painting, plus the HVAC contract moving to a repair line. Some is deferred work catching up rather than a new run rate.

buckets.name: Professional fees
buckets.read: Largest percentage move in the file, but on a small prior-year base - a timing effect as much as a cost increase. Confirm what the spend was for.

buckets.name: Marketing & advertising
buckets.read: Down, correctly, for a property that is full.

buckets.name: Turnover
buckets.read: Down sharply with retention. The clearest operational win of the year.

renewal.scenario_note: Assumes every move-out re-leases at the market assumption. Vacancy and downtime are charged inside NOI as an incremental vacancy haircut on the new run-rate (Inputs C28), stepping the asset from its TTM average physical vacancy of 2.07% to the 5.00% physical target in Inputs C9.
renewal.model_note: Recomputed live from unit level. Stabilised sensitivity, not a forecast: every move-out re-leases at the market assumption, and vacancy/downtime are charged as a recurring incremental-vacancy haircut on the new run-rate rather than one-time costs.

rollover.month: Expired before the rent roll month (holdover)

metrics.name: Physical occupancy
metrics.meaning: One vacant unit out of 263. Note 14 units carry move-out notices against six signed future leases, so forward exposure is real even though the snapshot is full.

metrics.name: Concessions as % of market rent
metrics.meaning: Effectively nil for a full year. The property fills units without buying occupancy.

metrics.name: Operating NOI margin (TTM)
metrics.meaning: Strong for stabilised multifamily. Every incremental rent dollar largely survives to the bottom line.

metrics.name: Turnover cost, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Down sharply as retention improved. Fewer turns is the cheapest expense saving there is.

metrics.name: Marketing spend, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Falling while occupancy holds. Reasonable for a property that is effectively full, though 14 notices are outstanding against six signed future leases.

metrics.name: Resident balances over 90 days, % of balances owed
metrics.meaning: Residential only. $3,586 aged past 90 days across 262 occupied units, on total resident balances of $57,198 - which is itself 4.6% of one month's rental income. Separately, the ground-floor retail tenant owes $5,040 of which 84% is over 90 days; that is a single commercial receivable and is excluded from every residential figure here.

metrics.name: Loss to lease (rent roll)
metrics.meaning: In-place rents sit far below the marked market. This is the single largest value item in the file.

metrics.name: Renewals priced below new leases
metrics.meaning: Renewals at +8% against new leases at +38%. The gap widens every month renewals are written soft.

metrics.name: Holdover units (lease already expired)
metrics.meaning: Residents past expiry on month-to-month. The cheapest part of the gap to approach, though a large increase can still trigger a move-out.

metrics.name: Operating expense growth, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Outpacing revenue growth on matching periods. Taxes, contract services and professional fees drive most of it; several are timing-affected.

metrics.name: Revenue growth, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Healthy in isolation. But marked market rent rose 25.3% over the same matching periods - $8.23M to $10.32M of monthly potential summed across Jan-Jul - so collected revenue is growing at roughly half the rate of the asking rent it is measured against. The gap is what renewals are leaving behind.

metrics.name: Non-controllable share of opex
metrics.meaning: Over half the cost base cannot be managed. It caps how much any expense program can deliver.

metrics.name: Professional fees, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: A very large percentage on a small prior-year base, so read the dollars not the percent. Still needs an explanation before it is treated as run-rate.

metrics.name: Administrative, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Driven by memberships and dues, licences and a new MIS line. Reviewable, not alarming.

metrics.name: Contract services, Jan-Jul 26 vs Jan-Jul 25
metrics.meaning: Elevator repairs and a new water quality contract. Check whether the elevator spend repeats.

metrics.name: Real estate tax accrual
metrics.meaning: The April entry is either a one-off or a catch-up and nobody has confirmed which. Worth about $287k of annual NOI.

metrics.name: Market rent basis
metrics.meaning: Yardi lifted every unit in one month. Loss to lease jumps for that reason, not because rents moved.

flags.why: The April entry is either a one-off supplemental or a catch-up to a permanently higher bill. The accrual was never changed, which points to a one-off but proves nothing. Around $287k of annual NOI either way.
flags.settle: The assessment notice or tax bill for the year beginning July 2026.

flags.why: Every one of the 263 units was marked up in a single month, median 15%, while in-place rent moved 6%. Loss to lease jumps from 19.5% to roughly 27% on that basis change alone.
flags.settle: Confirmation from the PM team that the new table reflects achievable rents.

flags.why: Renewals are being written at +8% into a market clearing at +38%. Every month at that level locks the gap in for another year.
flags.settle: The renewal notices actually going out, and at what increase.

flags.why: A credit of $26,972 makes economic occupancy print above 100% for the month. It is an accrual reversal, not an operating result. It inflates July NOI by $401,278 on an annualised basis - about $8.0M of value at a 5% cap - so any single-month annualisation off July overstates the asset. The Cover now carries an adjusted July column alongside the reported one, but the underlying entry is still unexplained.
flags.settle: Confirmation of what the reversal relates to.

flags.why: Up 1000% on one line. Left unexplained it will be underwritten as run-rate by a buyer.
flags.settle: An invoice-level breakdown of the increase.

flags.why: Repair costs rose from $8.6k to $45.8k while the maintenance contract fell. Could be a one-off failure or the start of a capital item.
flags.settle: Whether the work is complete and whether a replacement is coming.

flags.why: Physical vacancy moved from 4.56% in June, twelve units, to 0.38% in July, one unit. With two data points there is no trend, only a swing.
flags.settle: A monthly rent roll feed rather than ad hoc pulls.

flags.item: Renewal data not published at lease level
flags.why: The tracker charts renewals but does not expose the rows, so renewal analysis rests on a blended rate rather than unit detail.
flags.settle: A lease-level renewal export from the tracker owner.
